title: Keep the stock count right while stock moves

blocks.text: Pickers move stock between the bins of a warehouse all day, and every hour a job compares the warehouse's total with the books. Each bin is thread-safe on its own. The books are right, yet the hourly count sometimes reports a few units missing, and sometimes a few too many, always while stock is being moved.

Write `move(...)` and `total()` in `src/main/java/practice/Warehouse.java`, so that a move either happens whole or not at all, and a total taken at any moment, while moves run, equals the stock in the warehouse. About eight lines in total.
The tests use bins of their own, which can stop a call partway through, and run a move and a total against each other at that point.

cases.says: a move takes units from one bin and adds them to the other
a move of more units than the source holds is refused and changes neither bin
the total is the sum of every bin, before and after a move
a total taken while a move is between its two bins still counts the moved units exactly once
a move made while a total is reading the bins doesn't change the total it reports

origin.section: An Action Across Two Wallets Needs One Owner for Both Balances

concepts: An action or a read across two thread-safe objects is not atomic; the lock for a rule over both belongs to one object that owns both.
